revisions.reasoning: This causal edge is currently flagged NO_ID. Payments revenue is plausibly jointly determined with aggregate spending by omitted factors (business cycle, policy, payment adoption), so a time-series local-projection/IV design using clearly exogenous macro shocks already in the DAG can improve identification without changing the structural story.

identification_strategy.type: IV (shift-share / external shocks as instruments) + local projections
identification_strategy.argument: Instrument real_expenditure with external shocks that move Kazakhstan domestic demand but are plausibly exogenous to KSPI-specific payments revenue innovations: (i) oil_supply_shock and oil_demand_shock, (ii) vix_shock. Estimate pass-through using Jordà local projections with bank fixed effects (if panel) or controls for NBK rate and FX to isolate spending-driven volume effects.
identification_strategy.key_assumption: Oil/VIX shocks affect KSPI payments revenue only through aggregate spending/transaction volumes (and not through direct bank-specific pricing/fee changes conditional on FX and policy rate).

revisions.reasoning: NO_ID and magnitude_flag suggest confounding and/or scaling. Portfolio mix and RWA are jointly set with risk appetite, regulation, and growth opportunities. A policy-rule or quasi-exogenous reallocation shock is needed to defend causality.

identification_strategy.type: Instrumental variables (regulatory/eligibility shift) or diff-in-diff around risk-weight changes
identification_strategy.argument: Use a regulatory mapping/weights change (e.g., Basel/IRB parameters, risk-weight floors, SME/retail preferential weights) as an exogenous shifter of the RWA impact of a given portfolio mix. Implement diff-in-diff comparing exposures more vs less affected by the risk-weight change, or IV where the instrument is predicted RWA from lagged mix interacted with post-regulation indicator.
identification_strategy.key_assumption: Regulatory risk-weight change is exogenous to contemporaneous KSPI credit-risk shocks and affects RWA mechanically through weights rather than through simultaneous changes in underlying asset risk.

identification_strategy.type: IV using external shocks + distributed lag/local projections

Include NBK policy rate and FX as controls or mediators depending on estimand; prefer local projections with horizon h to map dynamics.
identification_strategy.key_assumption: Conditional on FX and policy-rate channels (if controlled), external shocks move COR primarily via real income (ability-to-pay) rather than via direct bank balance-sheet shocks.

identification_strategy.type: IV (external shocks) with controls for monetary/FX conditions
identification_strategy.argument: Instrument real_expenditure using oil_supply_shock, oil_demand_shock, and vix_shock. Estimate impact on ppop_kspi controlling for nbk_policy_rate and kzt_usd to separate pure demand/volume effects from margin/valuation effects.
identification_strategy.key_assumption: External shocks affect KSPI PPOP only through macro demand (and controlled monetary/FX channels), not through unobserved bank-specific operational shocks.

The derived node should be defined at the frequency of the econometric analysis (typically monthly/quarterly) by aggregating FX first, then interacting with the static share.

To resolve the frequency mismatch cleanly (and avoid ad-hoc implicit aggregation), add an explicit quarterly CPI aggregator node used by the real_expenditure identity. This improves structural soundness and auditability of derived variables.
